newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty to appreciate in long-term -premier.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty to appreciate in long-term -premier.

text.p: Poland's currency, the zloty, will continue to strengthen against a basket of Western currencies in the coming years, Polish Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz said on Friday.
Cimoszewicz told a news conference in the Baltic port of Szczecin that despite pressure from some lobby groups on the government to weaken the zloty, Poland would not change its exchange rate policy.

"Despite the effect the appreciation of the zloty has on the shipbuilding industry, the government does not envisge a change in the exchange rate policy in the coming years...the firming of the zloty will be a lasting phenomenon," he said.
The zloty rose more than 10 percent in real-terms last year under pressure from a huge current account surplus fuelled by unregistered cross-border trade estimated at about $3 billion.
However, the zloty's gains cut exporters' profits and hit hard some shipbuilders, who did not hedge against the exchange rate risk on lengthy contracts.
The Gdansk shipyard, one of the country's largest, was recently declared bankrupt after its debts exceeded 300 million zlotys.
The shipyard's officials said a large part of the debt was a result of the government's unfavourable exchange rate policy.
The exchange rate policy is in the discretion of the independent central bank, which, however, consults any major changes in the policy with the finance and foreign trade ministries.
The zloty is currently devalued by one percent a month against a basket of five currencies in a mechanism known as the crawling peg.
